Doubtful

/DOWT-fuhl/ - the first syllable rhymes with out · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Doubtful means uncertain or unlikely; open to question.

Given the engine's age and the spreading rust, it is doubtful the tractor will survive another harvest.

Worked Example

The permit officer was frank: with two failed kitchen checks on record, it was doubtful the food truck would be cleared for the festival season, however good its new menu.

Doubtful is milder and more exact than 'impossible' — it says the odds lean against a thing, or that a claim invites real questions, while leaving the door open a crack.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

questionable: inviting scrutiny, often about honesty or accuracy

unlikely: having low odds, plainly stated

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

certain: beyond question, fully settled

likely: expected to happen, with the odds in favor

Where it sits · how slim its chances look — iffy → doubtful → farfetched

iffy vs. doubtful: Iffy is looser and milder than doubtful — the odds wobble, but nobody is betting against it yet.

farfetched vs. doubtful: Farfetched goes further than doubtful, past shaky odds into something close to fantasy.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — doubt

Root — doubt: to waver between two (Latin dubitare, from duo, two)

Suffix — -ful

Suffix — -ful: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Doubt (from Latin dubitare, to waver between two) + -ful (full of) = full of wavering. Dubitare itself grew out of duo, 'two' — and a doubtful outcome still faces two ways.

Use the root in a new word: undoubtedly

Use the root in a new word: undoubtedly: She is undoubtedly the strongest swimmer on the team — nobody wavers on that.

Word Choice

Doubtful covers both the odds ('a comeback is doubtful') and the credibility ('a doubtful claim'). It is milder than 'impossible' and more committal than 'unsure' — the scale tips against, without the door quite closing.
